references.text: The only direct prophetic parallel in the OT that expresses a double resurrection: the righteous to life and the wicked to condemnation.

Jesus here describes the judgment over the two groups (the righteous and the unrighteous) with the same concept of eternal life versus eternal punishment, as a direct elaboration on the theme in John 5:29.
Jesus mentions here that the righteous will rise again for a recompense, which mirrors the contrast between resurrection to life and resurrection to judgment in John 5:29.
The same author (John) links belief in the Son's will to resurrection to eternal life, which is the positive part of the double resurrection in 5:29.
Jesus identifies himself as the resurrection and the life, and links faith in him to living even though one dies, which is the theological foundation for the resurrection to life in 5:29.
Peter refers to those who await a resurrection from the dead, distinguishing between those who are saved and those who are condemned, in line with the double resurrection.
